title: Finitely generated plane Cremona subgroups consisting entirely of algebraic elements have uniformly bounded degree
source_title: Finitely generated subgroups of algebraic elements of plane Cremona groups are bounded
author: Anne Lonjou; Piotr Przytycki; Christian Urech
difficulty_reason: The known rational-fibration alternative does not bound a finitely generated algebraic subgroup preserving a fibration, because its elements may affect different fibers. The authors identify the Jonquieres complex with a restricted product of fiber trees and prove that purely elliptic finite-generation actions fix a common point, controlling persistent fibers in both abelian and semisimple north-south cases. That new fixed-point core supplies boundedness after the classical Cremona and local-field prerequisites, beyond merely applying the fibration classification.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem1.1 over any fieldk: a finitely generated subgroup ofCr2(k) whose every element has bounded degrees of all iterates has uniformly bounded degree across the whole subgroup. Read full new Jonquieres/fiber-tree identification9–11 and all four cases of the restricted-product fixed-point proof11–15, with algebraic-element/automorphism context3–9. Cantat/Lamy reduction to a preserved rational fibration, Zariski factorization, decent tree actions and Druţu-Kapovich local-field embedding/unipotent-group results are expressly named prior foundations. No assumption that only the chosen generators are algebraic; every group element is required. No arbitrary higher-dimensional Cremona generalization or separate degree-growth corollary counted.
